transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ben Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Laura Kim (Cobalt CISO), Samir Patel (Head of Cloud), Devin Ross (Dir, SRE), Aisha Khan (Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): quick run through of incident response, rto/rpo, uptimesla numbers, escalation contacts, and KMS / encryption details. Customer asked about on-prem/private deployment options for sensitive workloads.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining; can you hear us okay?
[00:05] Laura (Cobalt): yes thanks, loud and clear, hi all.
[00:08] Maya: great, quick intro — i'm maya, AE, and ben is our se, priya on cs; we're here to walk through incident response and BCDR details tied to the SLA.
[00:18] Ben (Redwood): hi, i'll be the technical lead on this part. we'll cover detection, escalation, runbook steps, rto/rpo expectations, and how our platform interacts with customer kms and audit logs.
[00:28] Samir (Cobalt): sound good. high level, Cobalt's requirements are SOC2 compliance evidence, key management in our cloud KMS, rpo under 30 minutes for critical flows, rto under 4 hours, and clear escalation for sev1.
[00:40] Maya: perfect, that's super helpful. we'll flag where we can meet natively and where we'll need a private deployment or dedicated capacity.
[00:48] Devin (Cobalt): one small note — we expect a 99.95% uptime SLA for production endpoints, and a documented failover / region recovery plan.
[00:57] Priya (Redwood): noted, we have SLA tiers and we can provide historical uptime for the last 12 months; i'll pull that and include an addendum in the contract.

[02:10] Ben: jumping in — detection and monitoring: our runtime emits per-request telemetry, token latency histograms, and health checks. these feed into our metrics pipeline and we export metrics to prometheus/stackdriver / cloudwatch via integrations. we also support trace exports for request-level forensics.
[02:30] Laura: do you keep long-term audit logs? audit trails are a big ask — we need immutable logs for support audits and we need them to show who did what and when.
[02:40] Ben: yes, we capture immutable audit logs, retention is configurable by tier; hosted customers get 90 days by default, enterprise/private can configure longer retention or send to customer-owned s3/bucket. note the auto-transcript here: sometimes SAML spelled variously etc — forgive the audio.

[03:25] Samir: about keys — we need to manage keys via our cloud KMS (aws-kms). how does that work with your encryption at rest?
[03:33] Ben: we support customer-managed keys (CMK) with KMS integration. for hosted, we can either integrate with your cloud kms using an IAM role, or you can use a bring-your-own-key pattern in private deployments. key rotation is supported; we store only encrypted blobs and rotate via rewrap.
[03:50] Aisha (Cobalt): legal asks about breach notification SLAs — what's the timeline for notifying customers in case of a confirmed data exfil?
[03:57] Maya: standard is 72 hours for confirmed breaches to notify customers, we can negotiate tighter timelines in the enterprise contract; we'll surface our incident classification matrix.

[05:15] Ben: on incident classification — we operate sev levels: sev1 (complete outage impacting production), sev2 (degraded but functional), sev3 (minor/partial). for sev1 we aim for immediate pages and an initial response within 15 minutes.
[05:28] Devin: 15 minutes initial response is good. for sev1 we also need an incident commander and a runbook that lists recovery steps and owners. do you provide runbooks?
[05:35] Ben: yes, we provide runbook templates and example playbooks for typical failure modes: control plane outage, worker GPU node failures, disk corruption, kv-cache inconsistency, network partition. we'll share sanitized copies.

[06:40] Laura: RTO/RPO — i mentioned RPO under 30 minutes; can you confirm your backup cadence for logs and model state / kv caches?
[06:50] Ben: backups: persistent stores are snapshot-based every 15 minutes for critical flows (enterprise tiers) and hourly for standard. kv-cache is ephemeral; we offer checkpointing for session state per-customer on dedicated deployments. for hosted, we recommend design patterns to avoid single-point-of-state; or use dedicated capacity so checkpointing is available.
[07:05] Maya: to be clear, for the production LLM endpoints your rpo target depends on tier: enterprise can get RPO ~15 min with dedicated capacity and runbook, hosted standard is closer to 1 hour.

[08:20] Samir: and full failover — if a region goes down, can we fail over to another region with preserved session continuity?
[08:27] Ben: session continuity across regions is tough because of kv caches; we support cross-region replication for persistent stores, but live KV state usually cannot be fully preserved across region failover without design changes. for critical flows we suggest active-passive with replication and an RTO tested at 2-4 hours depending on data size.

[09:50] Devin: what's the typical SLA credit for missing 99.95%?
[09:55] Priya: our SLA has tiered credits — e.g. <99.9% gets 20% credit, <99.5% more. i'll send standard language; the enterprise addendum can change SLO targets.

[11:12] Laura: escalation chain — if we hit a sev1 after hours, what's the contact method? pagerduty? phone?
[11:18] Ben: primary is pagerduty with direct paging to on-call engineers. we also provide phone escalation and a dedicated slack or secure channel for enterprise customers. contact matrix will include on-call, escalation to se, then eng manager, then vp support.

[12:30] Maya: do you do tabletop exercises and periodic drills?
[12:34] Devin: we want a regular cadence, quarterly or semi-annual.
[12:37] Priya: yes, we run tabletop exercises with customers for enterprise contracts — we'll propose dates and a facilitator.

[14:00] Samir: about compliance evidence — we need SOC2 Type II report, ISO certs, pen test summaries, and any recent red team findings. do you red-team your infra?
[14:10] Maya: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation; pen test summaries are available for enterprise under NDA, and we can share a high level. we'll include these artifacts in the follow up.

[15:45] Laura: logging integrity: are logs tamper-evident? chain-of-custody?
[15:52] Ben: logs are append-only and we support WORM style export to customer buckets; we also publish signed digests for audit trails if required. retention and immutability are configurable in private/dedicated setups. hosted comes with common defaults.

[17:10] Aisha: on data residency — some customer data must remain in eu-only regions. how do you ensure data residency for EU customers?
[17:18] Ben: we have region-level deployments and you can restrict model placement and data residency policies. for regulated workloads we recommend private deployment or dedicated capacity pinned to a region.

[18:30] Devin: walk me through an actual incident example — say a GPU driver regression causes worker failures during peak. what's the sequence?
[18:38] Ben: typical flow: detection via health checks and increased error rates; automated auto-scaler pauses new sessions, alert routes to on-call; SE/engineer triages, if it's a driver issue we roll to previous known-good kernel, isolate bad nodes, evict failing containers, and bring up nodes in warm pool. communication: we open incident channel, post initial status within 15 minutes, update every 30 minutes until recovered, then 24-hour postmortem within 72 hours.

[20:02] Maya: also we have automatic fallbacks to smaller model variants in some setups to preserve availability during heavy load. that's part of graceful degradation policies.
[20:12] Samir: do fallbacks change SLA or accuracy requirements?
[20:16] Ben: no change in SLA for availability, but we document quality tradeoffs; customers can opt in-out of fallback behaviors.

[21:30] Laura: notification for regulatory breaches — we discussed 72 hours. can you provide your notification matrix with contacts and templates?
[21:38] Priya: yes — we have templated notifications (internal/external) and a matrix for timelines and legal escalation; we'll share redacted examples.

[23:00] Devin: backups restore time — can you restore a 2TB index and models in under 4 hours?
[23:07] Ben: 2TB restore depends on network egress and warm pools. with enterprise plan and dedicated replication we can meet a 4 hour RTO for that size; otherwise restoration may take longer. we'll run a capacity test during the pilot.

[24:30] Samir: what about chain-of-command for post-incident reviews? we want a single owner and 72-hour postmortem.
[24:38] Maya: agreed, we assign an incident commander for sev1 and deliver an RCA within 72 hours; a full detailed report follows within 2 weeks for major incidents.

[26:00] Laura: encryption in transit and at rest — any customer data cached for inference is encrypted?
[26:05] Ben: yes, tls in transit, at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys for enterprise; in hosted we encrypt with our KMS by default, or integrate with customer KMS on request. for session caches we encrypt in-memory and at rest snapshots.

[27:30] Devin: are there any single points of failure in your control plane?
[27:36] Ben: our control plane is multi-zone with leader election; it degrades gracefully. data plane is separate and can fail over. for guaranteed isolation we recommend dedicated capacity.

[29:00] Aisha: legal question — can we include a breach notification clause that requires Redwood to notify regulatory bodies as needed?
[29:08] Maya: we can include NDA/contract clauses for assisted regulatory notification; legal will coordinate offline with yours.

[30:30] Samir: what logging retention do you offer for audit logs on enterprise?
[30:35] Ben: enterprise: configurable to multi-year retention, we can ship to your s3 or to our long-term cold archive.

[31:55] Laura: regarding RBAC and SSO, we need SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO with enforced 2FA and role separation — can you support fine-grained roles?
[32:05] Ben: yes we support SAML, OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC with role templates and custom roles. we also support temporary elevated access for troubleshooting with audit logging.

[33:50] Maya: one more note — for private deployments we can offer additional controls: HSM integration, offline key storage, and air-gapped install options.

[35:00] Samir: timeline — if we do a pilot, what does a typical timeline look like for testing DR and tabletop?
[35:08] Priya: pilot typically 4-6 weeks: week 1 onboard and config, week 2 run integration tests and KMS setup, week 3 failover tests and a tabletop, week 4 evaluation and SLA sign-off.

[36:30] Devin: on escalation notifications — do you provide a runbook with exact command lines / steps? we prefer documented commands to avoid guesswork.
[36:38] Ben: yes I'll attach runbook steps including sample kubectl commands, scripts to rewrap keys, snapshot restore commands, and order of operations. some commands are redacted in hosted artifacts but full scripts are available in dedicated/private.

[38:10] Laura: breach disclosure — what is your contact for law enforcement or regulators if needed?
[38:16] Maya: legal escalation path will be Aisha on this call, then VP Legal, and we'll provide a 24/7 contact for high severity. we'll include this in the matrix.

[39:40] Samir: how do you validate backups? do you run restore rehearsals?
[39:45] Priya: yes, we recommend quarterly restore rehearsals for critical customers; Redwood can run them jointly with customer SREs.

[41:00] Devin: about metrics — what SLOs are available by default?
[41:05] Ben: default SLOs: p99 latency, request success rate, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, and regional availability. custom SLOs can be added in enterprise dashboards.

[42:30] Maya: any other questions before we recap next steps?
[42:35] Laura: a couple: can you confirm the RPO/RTO numbers again in writing? and share runbooks and SOC2?
[42:42] Maya: yes — we'll send RPO/RTO options: enterprise RPO 15 min (dedicated), RTO 2-4 hrs (tested), hosted RPO ~60 min, RTO 4-8 hrs.
[43:00] Priya: i'll include the SLA addendum and uptime history.

[44:20] Ben: last technical note — for model state we recommend designs that externalize critical session state to a replicated store to meet sub-30 min rpo.
[44:30] Devin: ok that makes sense.

[45:00] Maya: recap: maya sends SOC2/ISO artifacts; ben sends runbook and DR playbook; priya sends SLA addendum and uptime metrics; devin/share customer will confirm internal rto/rpo and contacts. schedule tabletop tentatively 2026-12-10.
[45:20] Laura: yep, we'll review and get back on dates.

[46:00] Aisha: legal will expect to review SLA language and breach notification templates.

[47:30] Samir: one more technical — do you support HSM integration for key wrapping?
[47:35] Ben: yes HSM supported in private/dedicated deployments and via KMS integrations in hosted with customer-managed keys.

[48:40] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with artifacts in the next 48 hours.
[48:48] Laura: thanks, bye.
[48:50] Devin: thanks.
